title: POC weekly sync - reliability incident follow-up
summary: Weekly POC sync to review the reliability incident from 2026-05-16. Discussed timeout patterns, bursts of 5xx, rate limiting windows, retry behavior, autoscaling thresholds. Agreement to run focused benchmark, adjust rate-limit backoff, and collect server-side traces. Redwood to share incident runbook and benchmark scripts.
next_steps: Redwood to share incident-runbook and logs link by 2026-05-19
Customer to run targeted benchmark using provided script and share results by 2026-05-22
SE to propose retry/backoff config and rate-limit window adjustments by 2026-05-21
Schedule follow-up deep-dive if new 5xxs appear
action_items: Priya Nair — collect and annotate server-side traces and correlate with cutover times; due 2026-05-21
Michael Lee — run benchmark with 95th pct latency workload and upload results; due 2026-05-22
Jamie Ortiz — send pricing/throughput summary and confirm Dedicated burst capacity options; due 2026-05-20
header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortiz (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood CSM), Michael Lee (StratoFin CTO), Natalie Gomez (StratoFin SRE), Arjun Patel (StratoFin Product), Samira Khan (StratoFin Eng)
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Ortiz: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I know we had the incident earlier this week so we'll focus on the follow-up. quick roll call?
[00:08] Michael Lee: Michael here.
[00:10] Natalie Gomez: Natalie - on call.
[00:12] Arjun Patel: Arjun.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood. Liam on?
[00:18] Liam Chen: Liam here.
[00:20] Jamie Ortiz: Great. quick agenda: recap incident timeline, dig into the 5xx / timeouts, talk retries and rate limits, and agree next steps.
[00:32] Michael Lee: yeah we saw a spike of 5xxs and timeouts around 09:40, client side saw a lot of 504s and our gateway started to throttle. seems tied to a burst of requests from a beta cohort.
[00:46] Natalie Gomez: the interesting bit was the burst triggered a cascade, our autop-scaler for the inference front-end didn't spin up fast enough, then requests queued and started hitting 5xx from the runtime, some looked like OOMs but traces are noisy.
[01:05] Priya Nair: thank you. from Redwood side we pulled logs — we see elevated tail latency at the same timestamp, and a pattern of rate-limit responses followed by retries from the client at t+10s which created a retry storm. there was also a short window where one of the replica pools reported intermittent NVID driver restarts — likely a noisy neighbor on the Dedicated pool, or a host-level transient.
[01:30] Arjun Patel: noisy neighbor okay. the test bed is on Dedicated dev pool, right? we thought Dedicated would be isolated.
[01:36] Jamie Ortiz: yes it's Dedicated dev, but depending on the provisioning we sometimes run on shared racks in that cluster for burst capacity. that burst capacity is what got used. the fallback routing tried a cheaper variant and we saw a model variant mismatch for a brief time which added extra recompile latency.
[01:55] Michael Lee: hmm that matches what we saw. is there any way to prevent the router from shifting variants mid-flight?
[02:02] Priya Nair: yes, you can pin model versions or disable variant fallback for a route; for the pilot we left fallback enabled to save cost during low load but during beta bursts it's risky. also we recommend prefix KV cache priming for the workload to keep KV cache warm — the cold KV cache caused extra decode work and higher p95.
[02:25] Natalie Gomez: can you explain the retry/backoff interaction? because our client retries 3 times with fixed delays and that seemed to amplify the issue.
[02:34] Priya Nair: right — fixed short retries against a tightening rate limit is the classic amplification. we suggest exponential backoff with jitter and circuit-breaker at the client side; on the server side we can help by returning a Retry-After header on 429s and smoothing the rate-limit windows (increase bucket size with slightly longer refill).
[02:55] Michael Lee: there's also a couple 5xx types: 502/503 and occasional 500. do you have a breakdown?
[03:02] Priya Nair: quick breakdown from the logs: 60% were 5xx code coming from the runtime (OOM-ish allocation failures), 25% were gateway 502s during the fallback routing transition, and 15% were proxy timeouts in the LB layer. I'll attach the histogram and raw logs link in the notes.
[03:22] Arjun Patel: OOMs — are we hitting max sequence length or batch size spikes? our traffic has longer contexts on a few requests.
[03:30] Priya Nair: appears correlated with a small fraction of requests with >2k token context and the batching window combined them into large batches. we had autoscaling thresholds low to reduce cost during the POC; that made the runtime hold onto larger batches longer and occasionally push memory over.
[03:48] Natalie Gomez: so two levers: reduce max batch size / cap request tokens or increase the autoscaling aggressiveness.
[03:55] Jamie Ortiz: yes — and also quantization profile and kernel selection can reduce memory footprint; Priya will recommend config. for immediate mitigation we can enforce a per-request token hard limit at the gateway and reject with a clear error to avoid downstream OOMs.
[04:12] Michael Lee: we can do that. we need clear error codes so our front-end shows proper messaging instead of retrying.
[04:18] Jamie Ortiz: we'll make sure the gateway returns 413-like semantic or a structured JSON with code and suggested action.
[04:26] Priya Nair: action: we'll supply patch for gateway error response and sample client-side retry policy.
[04:32] Liam Chen: also wanted to flag SLO impact — CSM note: we logged the incident in the portal, customers on the pilot impacted ~2.4% of requests during the 10m window.
[04:44] Arjun Patel: what about the NV driver restarts you mentioned — is that something you can mitigate or is it infra?
[04:50] Priya Nair: suspect hypervisor host issue; we'll escalate to infra ops, but we also have options: tolerate with more replicas, adjust host-affinity to avoid the noisy rack, or move to Dedicated isolated hosts (longer lead time).
[05:06] Michael Lee: cost tradeoff — moving to fully isolated hosts is fine but we need pricing.
[05:10] Jamie Ortiz: I'll include Dedicated burst and isolated-host pricing in the follow-up email.
[05:15] Natalie Gomez: on rate limits — our gateway saw a 429 spike before the 5xxs; is that because your rate limiter tightened as hosts went unhealthy?
[05:23] Priya Nair: yes, the rate limiter uses the healthy replica count to compute per-replica capacity. when a node went down the remaining replicas had lower headroom so clients started hitting 429s. smoothing the rate-limit refill and using a slightly larger token-bucket during transient failures prevents hard clamping.
[05:42] Arjun Patel: regarding metrics, we'd like end-to-end traces. can you share distributed traces?
[05:47] Priya Nair: yes — we'll share spans from gateway -> router -> runtime and annotate the traces with host IDs and model variant. expect a link in the runbook.
[05:57] Michael Lee: one more question on retries — our SDK retries on 5xx by default, can we configure so it doesn't retry on 502/503?
[06:04] Priya Nair: yes, you can set policy to only retry on idempotent endpoints and on 429/timeout with long backoff; we'll send recommended SDK config.
[06:14] Jamie Ortiz: cool. now let's confirm next steps and owners.
[06:18] Priya Nair: I will: 1) collect and annotate the traces, 2) provide suggested retry/backoff and gateway error patch, 3) propose autoscale tweaks and batch caps. due 2026-05-21.
[06:30] Michael Lee: I'll run the benchmark with the long-context workload and upload results by 2026-05-22.
[06:36] Jamie Ortiz: I'll send pricing options for isolated hosts and Dedicated burst capacity and include the incident runbook link by 2026-05-19.
[06:44] Liam Chen: I'll record the SLO impact in the CRM and update the pilot health dashboard.
[06:50] Arjun Patel: if we still see 5xx after these changes we'll schedule a deep SE-led session to run live repro.
[06:58] Jamie Ortiz: perfect. thanks all, we'll follow up via email and put the links in the calendar for checkpoint.
[07:05] Natalie Gomez: thanks.
[07:07] Michael Lee: thanks everyone.
[07:09] [END]
